eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Two
subtitle: Lesson 18 · Writing Data

eyebrow: Writes don't normally return rows -- OUTPUT does
caption: Inserts the row AND returns its new IDENTITY value -- no SCOPE_IDENTITY() needed.

code:
UPDATE dbo.LessonDemo
SET ListPrice = ListPrice * 1.10
OUTPUT deleted.ListPrice AS OldPrice, inserted.ListPrice AS NewPrice
WHERE Color = 'Red';
caption: UPDATE has both an old AND new value per row -- the only one that can reference both.
DELETE only has old values -- OUTPUT can only reference 'deleted' here.

code:
DELETE FROM dbo.LessonDemo
OUTPUT deleted.ProductID, deleted.ProductName, deleted.ListPrice
INTO dbo.LessonDemoArchive (ProductID, ProductName, ListPrice)
WHERE ListPrice < 500;
caption: Every deleted row lands in the archive table -- a permanent record, no second statement.
